articleHeadline: Genomic Copy Number Shifts Revealed in Plasmodium vivax Isolates From
articleSummary: Genome-wide CNV analysis of Plasmodium vivax from Northwestern India reveals CNVs linked to severe disease and drug resistance. In Bikaner, three cerebral malaria and three uncomplicated P. vivax isolates were analyzed using a custom 2×400K tiling array, confirming pure P. vivax infections. CNVs span all 14 chromosomes, affecting 2,138 genes, with sizes from ~100 bp to ~1.43 Mb; the largest CNV (~1.45 Mb) on chromosome 12 covers 316 genes. Large amplified blocks also occur on chromosomes 14 and 10. Notably, amplifications occur in three ABC transporter–family genes PVX_097025, PVX_080100, PVX_118100, and pvmdr1, consistent with mefloquine/artesunate resistance signals; chloroquine resistance markers show chr12 amplification and chr1 deletion. Surface antigens show extensive CNVs: all 24 tryptophan-rich antigens (TRAgs) amplified, PVX_088850 linked to PvMSP7; 23 serine-repeat antigens on chromosome 4, with 19 deletions. These patterns suggest genome-wide diversification impacting virulence and drug tolerance, within an endemic Indian setting.

articleHeadline: Sandwich ELISA Offers Rapid Antigen Test for Feline Coronavirus Detection
articleSummary: Fujian, China, researchers developed and validated a double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA) that detects the feline coronavirus (FCoV) spike protein directly in feline fecal samples and ascitic fluid, providing a low-cost, high-throughput alternative to RT-qPCR. articleHeadline: Gut Bacterium E. coli Emerges as a Central Suspect in IgA Nephropathy
articleSummary: IgA nephropathy (IgAN), the globe’s most common primary glomerular disease, shows striking geographic variation with Japan: ~39–45 per million; France: ~25–31; China comprising ~30–40% of primary glomerular diseases in biopsies. articleSummary: Chikungunya infection persists in Kerala for two decades as Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus breeding remains uncontrolled. First reported in Alappuzha (2006), the outbreak spread to coastal districts Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram, with Cherthala seeing early deaths. In Aug–Sep 2006, about 70,000 sought treatment; more than 90 died, and by October deaths exceeded 100. In 2007, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, and Idukki were affected, ultimately spreading across Kerala, with over 500,000 people infected. Severe joint and muscle pain caused walking difficulties, and many patients experienced prolonged pain despite treatment; no antiviral drug has been identified, leaving mosquito control as the sole preventive measure. Africa-origin tracing: Tanganyika reported in 1952, virus identified in 1955; the name Chikungunya derives from an African term describing bent posture due to painful joints.
notes: 記事は2006年のアラップーザ発生から2007年にかけてのケーララ州全域への流行拡大を振り返る歴史的特集記事であり、現在の感染状況や新規症例データは報告されていない。コンゴ民主共和国やタンガニーカへの言及もチクングニアウイルスの起源（1952年アフリカ）に関する歴史的背景説明であり、現在の発生国ではない。

articleHeadline: Indonesia's Tuberculosis Genomes Point to Fresher Drug Targets
articleSummary: Indonesia's tuberculosis burden remains high, with 444 Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Java and Papua analyzed. MDR-TB accounts for 28.2% of isolates; 5.4% are pre-extensively drug-resistant. Predicted resistance is highest for rifampicin (41.2%) and isoniazid (36.7%), while no isolates show mutations to bedaquiline, linezolid, clofazimine, or delamanid. Lineage 2 (East-Asian) makes up 46.2% of samples and carries the bulk of resistance: only 35.6% pan-susceptible vs 59.8% (Lineage 4) and 83.9% (Lineage 1). Lineage 2 accounts for 65.6% of MDR and 70.8% of pre-XDR isolates. The study compared ten classical resistance genes against ten emerging metabolic drug-target genes (purine, folate, biotin, shikimate, etc.). Across 435 isolates, classical loci were less conserved (mean 96.47%) than emerging targets (99.24%), with higher SNP density in classical genes. pncA and katG show strongest drug-pressure signals.

articleSummary: Bangkok temple stray cats harbor Giardia duodenalis, strains shared with humans, in a 2015 study across 43 temples in 24 districts. Feline assemblage F occasionally found in Thai humans. Adjusted odds of Giardia positivity were higher in cats with no human contact (aOR 8.80; 95% CI 2.15–35.98), though this is exploratory (n=15 feral). Methods used SSU rRNA nested PCR and genotyping at gdh and tpi.

articleSummary: Meningococcal disease (Neisseria meningitidis) is a rapid, potentially fatal infection that can progress to meningitis or septicemia. Close contacts should be considered for antibiotic prophylaxis, ideally within 24 hours of case identification, to reduce carriage and transmission. Vaccination may be indicated, but protection varies by serogroup (A, B, C, W, Y) and is not absolute. Monitor symptoms for 10 days after last exposure; infants may show poor feeding. Seek urgent care for warning signs: high fever with severe headache, neck stiffness, persistent vomiting, lethargy, seizures, rapid breathing, cool or pale extremities, or a non‑blanching purpuric rash. Emphasize hygiene and coordinate vaccination with health authorities and schools.

articleSummary: China multicenter study enrolled 143 patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis or schistosomiasis-related cirrhosis across three institutions from Aug 2019 to Dec 2021. Researchers applied radiomics to non-contrast CT liver images plus basic clinical data to distinguish etiologies non-invasively. Feature selection used mRMR and LASSO to produce a Rad-score. Three models were built: clinical, radiomics, and integrated. The integrated model achieved AUCs of 0.990 (training), 0.920 (internal validation), and 0.782 (external validation); external drop reflects cross-site variability. Schistosomiasis-related fibrosis concentrates periportal around portal veins, whereas HBV cirrhosis shows diffuse parenchymal damage; Rad-score differed significantly (p<0.001). The integrated model offered the greatest clinical utility per decision curve analysis and showed good calibration, supporting a noninvasive approach to guide treatment decisions—such as antiparasitic therapy for schistosomiasis—in regions where both diseases coexist.

Primary symptoms include chronic cough (with or without sputum), fever and chills, shortness of breath, chest pain, loss of appetite and weight, and night sweats. articleSummary: Plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, results in about 600 cases annually worldwide. Diagnosis is confirmed by detecting the bacteria in lymph node fluid, blood, or sputum, guiding immediate therapy. articleSummary: Rotavirus remains the leading cause of diarrhea-related hospitalizations among children under five in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, based on a two-year, hospital-based surveillance (2017–2018) at two hospitals. Rotavirus was detected in 39% of samples in 2017 and 37% in 2018, confirming its prominence. Other frequent pathogens included adenovirus 40/41 (28% in 2017; 3% in 2018), EAEC (27% in 2017; 28% in 2018), and norovirus GII (11% in 2017; 10% in 2018). Among rotavirus-positive samples, coinfection occurred in 81% (2017) and 74% (2018), with bacteria most commonly co-detected. A key limitation is that coinfections were recorded as individual pathogens rather than analyzed as a separate category, limiting assessment of their contribution to disease severity. These findings underscore the dynamic, multi-pathogen etiology of pediatric diarrhea in the region.

articleSummary: Russia’s frozen hinterlands harbor disease risks. articleHeadline: Trivalent Antiviral Conjugates Trap Influenza Viruses by Cross-Linking Them
articleSummary: Influenza antiviral strategy expanded with multivalent antiviral conjugates (AVCs) tethered to an Fc fragment, developed by researchers from the Academy of Military Medical Sciences in Beijing with Tsinghua University, Xiamen University and the University of Hong Kong. Using click chemistry, the team built mono-, di-, and tri-valent zanamivir-Fc (AVC-Z1–Z3) and a tri-valent peramivir-Fc (AVC-P3). Tri-valent AVC-Z3 showed superior antiviral activity and, crucially, induced inter-virion aggregation by cross-linking neuraminidase-bearing virions, producing a dual-stage inhibition that blocks both entry and release. AVC-P3 displayed stronger in vitro activity and a longer in vivo half-life than AVC-Z3 and CD388 with YTE. In mouse models challenged with H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, and influenza B, AVC-P3 outperformed other AVCs, baloxavir, and CD388, suggesting broad, long-acting prophylactic/therapeutic potential against diverse influenza A and B threats.
